citations.quote: I got an email from the Gerance yesterday saying the building is being sold and that my "rental relationship ends on 31 July 2027"
I really don't know if that counts as a termination or if they've actually terminated yet or if it's just a heads-up
rent's all paid, no arrears, so it's not that
if it's real I'd need longer to move, I'm recovering from a knee operation and can't carry anything or look at flats properly until spring

plan.because: Required if a termination notice was received; that defining event is expressly unresolved.
The customer reports an email but is unsure whether it is a termination; the original has not been supplied.
Deadline evidence applies if receipt of a termination notice is established.
Applicability depends on the unresolved termination-notice receipt.
The reported sale is not the original statement of grounds; this evidence applies if notice receipt is established.
A family home is not mentioned and is presumed absent for planning; living alone does not independently establish marital status.
Retaliation is unmentioned and presumed absent for planning.
Hardship and a need for more time are reported, but the extension node depends on the unresolved notice receipt.
This document is optional under the process.

questions: Please clarify promptly whether the email itself purports to terminate the tenancy or is only advance information. What is its exact wording?
On what date did you receive the email, and have you received any other termination communication or official form? The receipt date may be important for a challenge deadline.
